## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished presentation. To learn more about Quarto presentations see <https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/>.

## Bullets

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes:

-   Content authored with markdown
-   Output from executable code

## Code

When you click the **Render** button a presentation will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggokabeito)
library(knitr)
library(RCurl)
library(kableExtra)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggrepel)
library(DAAG)
library(FactoMineR)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false

c1 <- getURL("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/division-zero/Data-608/refs/heads/main/Story%205/train%20(1).csv")
#read in the raw file
train_df <- data.frame(read.csv(text = c1 ))
#put the csv into a dataframe

head(train_df)
```

```{r}

numeric_cols <- sapply(train_df, is.numeric)
train_df[numeric_cols] <- lapply(train_df[numeric_cols], function(x) {
 x[is.na(x)] <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
 x
})

```

```{r}
train <- read.csv(text = c1)
train2 <- read_csv(c1)

train_df <- train_df %>% select(-Alley)


train_df2 <- na.omit(train_df)



train_fit =  train_df |>
 select(where(is.numeric)) |>
 prcomp(scale = TRUE)

```

```{r}
summary(train_fit)
```

```{r}
train_fit |> augment(train_df)
```

```{r}
train_mca =  train_df |>
 select(!where(is.numeric)) |>
MCA( ncp = 10, graph = TRUE)

train_mca |> summary()

```

```{r}


train_mca$var$contrib[, 1]

# Sort to find the most important variables
sort(train_mca$var$contrib[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)


```

```{r}
sort(train_mca$var$contrib[, 2], decreasing = TRUE)

```

```{r}

sort(train_mca$var$contrib[, 3], decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}

head(train_mca$var$coord)

```

```{r}

head(train_mca$var$contrib)

sort(train_mca$var$contrib[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)

contrib_df <- as.data.frame(train_mca$var$contrib)
contrib_df$category <- rownames(contrib_df)


contrib_df$variable <- sub("_.*", "", contrib_df$category)
sort(contrib_df$variable[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)

contrib_df  |> 
 group_by(variable)  |> 
   summarise(total_contrib = sum(`Dim 1`))  |> 
arrange(desc(total_contrib))

contrib_df  |> 
 group_by(variable)  |> 
   summarise(total_contrib = sum(`Dim 2`))  |> 
arrange(desc(total_contrib))

contrib_df  |> 
 group_by(variable)  |> 
   summarise(total_contrib = sum(`Dim 3`))  |> 
arrange(desc(total_contrib))

```

```{r}
train_fit |>
 augment(train_df, color = Foundation) %>%
ggplot(aes(.fittedPC1, .fittedPC2)) +
 geom_point(size = 1.5) +
 scale_color_manual(
 values = c(m = "#D55E00", f = "#0072B2")
 ) +
 theme_minimal(base_size=16) +
 labs(title="PCA Coordinates for Australian Athletes",
 x = "PC 1", y= "PC 2",subtitle = "Color shows sex")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7

arrow_style <- arrow(
  angle = 20, length = grid::unit(8, "pt"),
  ends = "first", type = "closed"
)
train_fit %>%
  tidy(matrix = "rotation")  |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = "PC", values_from = "value",
    names_prefix = "PC"
  )  |> 
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_segment(
    xend = 0, yend = 0,
    arrow = arrow_style
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = column), hjust = 1,vjust=1) +
  xlim(-0.5, 0.5) + ylim(-0.25, 0.75) + 
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal(base_size =16)
```
